walkthroughs.body_html:
Communication, Homeostasis & Energy — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Communication, Homeostasis & Energy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Communication, Homeostasis & Energy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Approximate energy transfer between consumer trophic levels is:
Eutrophication leads to fish kills mainly because of:
options: Toxic algae
Reduced dissolved oxygen
Excess sunlight
Low temperatures

mcqs.q: Why are food chains usually limited to about 4 or 5 trophic levels?
options: Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
Only ~10 percent of energy is transferred between trophic levels; eventually too little energy remains to support another level.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
There aren't enough types of animals to fill more trophic levels.

mcqs.q: What does negative feedback do in homeostasis?
options: It reverses a change in a controlled variable, bringing it back towards the set point.
Negative feedback makes a process get worse or amplifies the change.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.

mcqs.q: Why is negative feedback the default mechanism in homeostasis?
options: Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
Negative feedback amplifies changes to make them more noticeable.
Negative feedback only operates when something goes wrong in the body.
It opposes deviations from a set point, returning the variable toward its normal value — keeping internal conditions stable.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Producer”?
options: Energy passed to next trophic level as a percentage; about 10% between consumers, lower for producers.
Autotroph that converts light or chemical energy into biomass; e.g. plants, algae.
Cycling of nitrogen via fixation (Rhizobium), nitrification (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter), denitrification and decomposition.
Enrichment of waters with nutrients causing algal blooms, decomposition by bacteria and O₂ depletion.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Energy transfer efficiency”?
options: Cycling of nitrogen via fixation (Rhizobium), nitrification (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter), denitrification and decomposition.
A feeding level within an ecosystem; producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, etc.
NPP = GPP − R, energy available to next trophic level after respiratory losses.
Energy passed to next trophic level as a percentage; about 10% between consumers, lower for producers.
